title: Openings & endings
examples: What makes a good opening sentence?
How can I make my story start exciting?
Can you show me how to end a piece with a circular ending?

explain.say: Today we are learning about making strong openings and endings.
A hook is a sentence that grabs the reader's attention immediately.
For example, instead of saying the sun rose, try this hook.

draw.text: Example: The sun painted the sky.

explain.say: A circular ending brings the reader back to the beginning idea.
For instance, if you started with a lonely boat, end with the boat.
In real life, you use this when writing a persuasive speech.

faq.q: What is the difference between a hook and a topic sentence?
faq.a: A hook is designed to grab attention right away. A topic sentence introduces the main idea of a paragraph.
asks: How do I start a paragraph strongly?
Is a hook always a question?

faq.q: Does a circular ending mean I repeat the exact same words?
faq.a: No, it means revisiting the idea or theme from the start, not copying words exactly.
asks: Can I just mention the beginning thing at the end?
What if the beginning and end are about different things?

faq.q: Should I use a hook every time I write something?
faq.a: It is very helpful for longer pieces like essays or stories. Shorter pieces might need a different opening.
asks: Is it mandatory to have a hook?
When is a hook most useful?

faq.q: Can I use a surprising fact as a hook if it is not true?
faq.a: No, your opening hook must be accurate information. Always stick to facts you know are correct.
asks: Can I make up a fact to start?
Is it okay to exaggerate a fact?

faq.q: If I use a circular ending, does my writing feel confusing?
faq.a: Not if the connection is smooth. The reader should feel a sense of completion or circle back to thought.
asks: How do I make the return feel natural?

facts: A hook is the very first sentence or idea of a piece.
A circular ending echoes the main theme or image from the start.
Starting with a question can engage the reader's curiosity.
The goal of both techniques is reader engagement.

quiz.say: If you start by describing a quiet forest, what should a circular ending do?
quiz.show: End by referencing the quiet forest.

options.show: Talk about a completely new topic.
options.say: Talk about a completely new topic.

options.show: Mention the silence of the trees again.
options.say: Mention the silence of the trees again.

quiz.why: A circular ending brings the reader back to the initial setting or idea, like the forest's silence.

wrong.0: This creates a sudden jump and leaves the reader feeling disconnected from the start.
wrong.1: While summarizing is good, it doesn't create the thematic loop of a circular ending.
wrong.2: This breaks the tone and the established theme of the writing piece.

quiz.say: Which sentence best creates a hook?

options.show: B. Jupiter is the biggest planet.
options.say: B. Jupiter is the biggest planet.

options.show: C. The solar system is big.
options.say: C. The solar system is big.

options.show: What if the sky held secrets we could never see?
options.say: What if the sky held secrets we could never see?

quiz.why: This question immediately makes the reader curious about hidden things in the sky.

wrong.0: This is a simple fact that the reader might already know.
wrong.1: This is too vague and does not give the reader a specific point of interest.
wrong.3: This is purely informative and lacks any emotional pull for the reader.
